This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Shivaraj in a motor vehicle accident dated 24.02.2017.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the wife, children, mother and brother of deceased Shivaraj.
It is the case of the petitioners that on 24.02.2017 at 4-30 p.m., deceased was proceeding by walk on Ekamba-Ganeshpur road of Ekamba village.
At that time, driver of vehicle bearing registration No.KA-34/M-5093 ('offending vehicle' for short), came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the accident, he sustained injuries and died on the spot.

As the owner and insurer respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.
6. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.
As there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
8. Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and one witness as P.W.2.
Exs.P1 to 16 are marked.
9. Respondent No.2 has not led any oral or documentary evidence.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.9,18,000/- with interest at 8% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

11. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.7,68,000/-
 2. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

3 . Loss of consortium Rs.1,20,000/-
 4. Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
12. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
13. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under other heads also requires enhancement and prays to allow the appeal.
14. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, Shivaraj died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.
17. In the post mortem report, the age of the deceased is noted as 29 years.
However, considering the age of the children, the Tribunal has held that the deceased might have been 34-35 years when the accident took place and therefore taken 16 as the multiplier.
There is no basis for such speculation.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered as 29 years and multiplier 17.

3 absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income of notional basis.

sentences.text:
Since the accident is of the year 2017, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/-
p.m. instead of Rs.6,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was below the age of 40 years, 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case).

sentences.text:
Therefore,
the income is (2018) 18 SCC 130 required to be taken at Rs.14,350/-.
Respondent No.5 being adult brother of the deceased cannot be considered as dependent.

During the pendency of the petition,
petitioner No.4 died.
Therefore, 1/3rd is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses of the deceased.

With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.14,350 x 12 x 17 x 2/3 =
19,51,600/-.

Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,51,600/- as against Rs.7,68,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
18.
As wife and children of the deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each and rightly the Tribunal has granted Rs.1,20,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses.

19. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.21,01,600/- as against Rs.9,18,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No. awarded by the awarded by  Tribunal this Court  1. Towards loss Rs.7,68,000/- Rs.19,51,600/-
 of dependency

2 . Loss of estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 3. Loss of Rs.1,20,000/- Rs.1,20,000/-
 consortium

4. Funeral Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 expenses

Since without any basis, the Tribunal has granted interest at 8% and in the light of decision in MFA No.103557/2016 dated 20.03.2018, the same is reduced to 6% and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part.
b. Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.21,01,600/- together with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.9,18,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

c. Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6%
p.a. (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
